To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) methane emission rates at gathering facilities ranged from 0 to 700 kg/h (0 to 600 scfm) with an average of 20 kg/h (17 scfm); (ii) normalized methane emission rates (as a percentage of methane throughput) were generally less than 1%; (iii) methane emission rates were negatively correlated with throughput, with the highest emission rates at the smallest facilities; (iv) the highest emissions were associated with venting from liquids handling systems and

1) the distribution of measured emission rates is skewed, with 30% of the facilities contributing 80% of total emissions, and that 2) normalized emissions rates (i.e., emissions per throughput) are negatively correlated with throughput and are higher at facilities with substantial venting.
• Methane emissions rates at G&P facilities ranged from 0–700 kg/h (0–600 scfm) and were highly skewed, with a median of 5.5 kg/h (4.7 scfm) and a 90th percentile of 30 kg/h (25 scfm).

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is significant variation in methane emissions from gathering facilities, and that a small subset of these facilities are responsible for a disproportionate share of the total emissions.
methane emissions from G&P facilities can be very high, but that the vast majority of emissions are low.
